messages.text:
At home power the sats usually come to less than the electricity — that's not why people buy it. You're buying a draw at a full 3.125 BTC block every ten minutes for years, steady sats to your own wallet meanwhile, and a real piece of the network you can watch run.

Still weighing the BC04, or thinking bigger?
BC04  is max I can afford.
Read the hammer miner bc04 page
Searched the catalog · Hammer Miner (postal code ····)/s

The B.04 is a solid pick at $239 — 6 TH/s, 100 W, about 50 dB, so it can sit on a desk. In stock, ships within 5 business days. It's the cheapest real way into Bitcoin mining and the block draw runs every ten minutes regardless.

Want me to build the cart?

Then the honest move is a second BC04 — same price, doubles your hashrate and doubles your block odds, and it's the best value you can get at that budget. Nothing else under $239 beats it per TH.

Want it in the cart, or are you happier waiting and saving toward a B30?
I don't have enough electricity to run second BC04.

Then don't force it. The one option that fits both limits is the Thor X1 — $219, 3.2 TH/s on about 25 W, USB-C powered, so a quarter of the BC04's draw. Half the hashrate, but it adds a real second ticket for ~$3.60 a month in power at your rate.

Otherwise running the one BC04 is a perfectly good answer.

context.pop: Looking for a home Bitcoin miner? I can help you pick one.
